# Reference versus second render, approximate normalized image coordinates:
# - Column foot: reference (.72,.84), render (.76,.82); its color boundary is
#   at reference y=.47, render y=.55. The column overlaps the rear furniture.
# - Rear lockers: reference roughly x=.40-.63, y=.39-.61; render approximately
#   x=.36-.59, y=.44-.62, behind the bunk.
# - Bunk front upright: reference near x=.40, y=.32-.70; render near x=.32,
#   y=.42-.76. Both show pale mattresses separated by dark gaps.
# - Foreground left equipment: reference x=0-.20, y=.48-.72; the render clips
#   most of it at the left edge. The left bench recedes diagonally toward the bunk.
# - Right wall board: reference x=.77-.90, y=.34-.46; render is almost entirely
#   cropped. The red wall object is likewise cropped at the right edge.
# - Nearest lamp: reference center about (.39,.16); render center about
#   (.33,.30). Ceiling structures reach the upper frame in both images.
# Vertical posts are nearly vertical; bench edges recede toward the center.
# The rendered floor is much lighter and more uniform than the reference.
#
# Ranked corrections and predicted effects:
# 1. Move the right wall fixtures onto a front-facing wall return: the dark board
#    and red object move left into view and grow in visible area.
# 2. Move the column left and raise its paint boundary: its shaft and foot move
#    left, while the brown/cream transition moves upward.
# 3. Shift the bunk front frame right and extend its posts upward, bringing the
#    high-contrast frame closer to its reference silhouette. Shift lockers right
#    and raise their tops locally. Preserve their overlap and mattress gaps.
# 4. Move the nearest hanging lamp toward the camera and raise it; its shade
#    becomes larger and moves upward. Bring the heater and foreground cabinet
#    farther into the image. Darken the floor and moderate ambient lighting;
#    apparent brightness also depends on the lights and surface orientation.
# Camera is retained because foreground and background errors are inconsistent.
# The program prints a small camera trial and restores the original camera.
# Inventory: room, beams and pipes, column, bunk and bedding, lockers, table,
# chair, benches, foreground equipment, heater, wall board, fire equipment,
# notice and hanging lamps. Hidden depths and rear furniture remain uncertain.
# Expanded primitive estimate: architecture 9, column 3, bunk 26, lockers 28,
# equipment 26, benches 10, furniture 12, heater 7, wall fixtures 8,
# overhead 17, lamps 9: approximately 155 separate meshes.

from sceneact import *
import bpy
from mathutils import Vector

scene = Scene('Utility bunk room')
cream = (.61, .60, .52)
wall = (.70, .69, .61)
floor_color = (.19, .055, .033)
brown = (.23, .065, .038)
black = (.018, .023, .020)
dark = (.035, .045, .038)
metal = (.34, .37, .35)
green = (.018, .075, .055)

def add(parent, name, shape):
    parent.include(name, shape)

# Independent major dimensions, positions, and camera parameters.
ROOM_WIDTH, ROOM_DEPTH, ROOM_HEIGHT = 5.8, 12.0, 3.35
COLUMN_X, COLUMN_Y, COLUMN_TRANSITION = .90, -.65, 1.85
BUNK_X0, BUNK_X1 = -2.30, -.54
BUNK_Y0, BUNK_Y1 = .55, 4.12
CAMERA_POSITION = (0.0, -7.7, 2.05)
CAMERA_TARGET = (0.0, 2.1, 1.55)
CAMERA_LENS = 48

room = Asset('Architecture')
add(room, 'floor', box((ROOM_WIDTH, ROOM_DEPTH, .12),
    center=(0,1.1,-.06), color=floor_color))
add(room, 'rear_wall', box((ROOM_WIDTH,.14,ROOM_HEIGHT),
    center=(0,5,1.675), color=cream))
add(room, 'left_wall', box((.14,ROOM_DEPTH,ROOM_HEIGHT),
    center=(-2.9,1.1,1.675), color=cream))
add(room, 'right_wall', box((.14,5.4,ROOM_HEIGHT),
    center=(2.9,2.3,1.675), color=wall))
# A short front-facing return gives the right wall objects their visible face.
add(room, 'right_return', box((1.35,.12,3.35),
    center=(2.48,2.9,1.675), color=wall))
add(room, 'ceiling', box((ROOM_WIDTH,ROOM_DEPTH,.12),
    center=(0,1.1,3.36), color=(.43,.35,.28)))
add(room, 'rear_baseboard', box((ROOM_WIDTH,.06,.28),
    center=(0,4.91,.14), color=brown))
add(room, 'left_baseboard', box((.06,10,.27),
    center=(-2.81,1,.135), color=brown))
add(room, 'return_baseboard', box((1.35,.05,.27),
    center=(2.48,2.82,.135), color=brown))
scene.include('architecture', room)

pillar = Asset('Front support column')
add(pillar,'upper',rod(.145,start=(COLUMN_X,COLUMN_Y,COLUMN_TRANSITION),
    end=(COLUMN_X,COLUMN_Y,3.35),color=(.76,.74,.65)))
add(pillar,'lower',rod(.145,start=(COLUMN_X,COLUMN_Y,.05),
    end=(COLUMN_X,COLUMN_Y,COLUMN_TRANSITION),color=brown))
add(pillar,'foot',rod(.20,start=(COLUMN_X,COLUMN_Y,.015),
    end=(COLUMN_X,COLUMN_Y,.07),color=(.34,.23,.17)))
scene.include('support_column',pillar)

bunk = Asset('Left bunk beds')
for x in (BUNK_X0,BUNK_X1):
    for y in (BUNK_Y0,BUNK_Y1):
        add(bunk,'post_%s_%s'%(x,y),rod(.036,
            start=(x,y,.05),end=(x,y,2.55),color=black))
for z in (.43,1.00,1.57,2.05):
    for x in (BUNK_X0,BUNK_X1):
        add(bunk,'long_rail_%s_%s'%(z,x),rod(.025,
            start=(x,BUNK_Y0,z),end=(x,BUNK_Y1,z),color=black))
    for y in (BUNK_Y0,BUNK_Y1):
        add(bunk,'end_rail_%s_%s'%(z,y),rod(.025,
            start=(BUNK_X0,y,z),end=(BUNK_X1,y,z),color=black))
for i,z in enumerate((.49,1.06,1.63)):
    add(bunk,'mattress_%d'%i,box((1.58,3.15,.11),
        center=(-1.42,2.37,z),color=(.64,.65,.59)))
    add(bunk,'pillow_%d'%i,box((1.12,.50,.10),
        center=(-1.42,3.62,z+.10),color=(.76,.76,.70)))
scene.include('bunk',bunk)

lockers = Asset('Rear gray lockers')
for i in range(4):
    x = -.65+i*.42
    add(lockers,'body_%d'%i,box((.40,.43,1.95),
        center=(x,4.65,1.285),color=metal))
    add(lockers,'door_%d'%i,box((.36,.025,1.83),
        center=(x,4.425,1.30),color=(.44,.47,.44)))
    add(lockers,'handle_%d'%i,box((.028,.035,.15),
        center=(x+.13,4.398,1.25),color=dark))
    for k in range(4):
        add(lockers,'vent_%d_%d'%(i,k),box((.22,.016,.018),
            center=(x,4.394,1.85-k*.065),color=(.22,.24,.22)))
scene.include('lockers',lockers)

cabinet = Asset('Left foreground equipment')
add(cabinet,'body',box((.86,1.82,1.28),
    center=(-2.12,-.15,.72),color=(.045,.065,.058)))
add(cabinet,'top',box((.98,1.98,.08),
    center=(-2.12,-.15,1.39),color=dark))
for j in range(3):
    yy=-.75+j*.57
    add(cabinet,'panel_%d'%j,box((.025,.48,.95),
        center=(-1.68,yy,.76),color=(.065,.09,.08)))
    for k in range(7):
        add(cabinet,'louver_%d_%d'%(j,k),box((.018,.39,.022),
            center=(-1.66,yy,.42+k*.10),color=(.16,.19,.17)))

# Reference inventory and comparison, normalized image coordinates:
# Architecture: cream ceiling and upper walls, yellow lower walls, light tiled
# floor, and windows and doors along both sides. Wall and floor edges converge
# toward the stage; reference ceiling fans partly cross the top crop.
# Stage: reference about (.37,.24)-(.66,.43), last render about
# (.40,.31)-(.60,.46). The rendered dark recess is too small and low.
# Board: reference about (.48,.33)-(.58,.41), render about (.46,.38)-(.55,.44).
# Foreground left desk: reference about (.14,.59)-(.37,.89), render about
# (.25,.62)-(.40,.83). Foreground right desk: reference about (.51,.55)-(.70,.82),
# render about (.55,.62)-(.70,.80). Desks overlap benches and bags; rear desks
# become densely occluded. The rendered benches have overly solid supports.
# Reference nearest windows start near x=.04, y=.18; rendered window frames
# start around x=.15, y=.28. Their precise depths and correspondences are uncertain.
# Reference floor has a varied, warm tile pattern; the last render is flatter.
#
# Largest supported corrections:
# 1. Increase lens from 23 to 27 mm and lower target slightly: background stage
#    and window corners should spread outward and move upward, while foreground
#    objects spread outward. The small projection trial below checks direction.
# 2. Make the curtain nearly black and widen its stage locally, retaining red
#    highlights and green wings. The dark rear region should occupy more area.
# 3. Move the nearest left desk left and widen it, moving its outline toward
#    (.14,.59)-(.37,.89). Replace solid bench supports with thin legs to restore
#    the visible gaps. Darken desk surfaces; their brightness also depends on light.
# 4. Move nearest fans toward the camera to put their silhouettes near the top
#    crop, and add warm floor-tile variation. Side opening depth is uncertain.
#
# Approximate expanded primitive count: room 6, floor joints 42, openings 68,
# stage 16, desks 28*9=252, bags 24, fans 20, other fittings 15: about 443.
# Each room, desk, bag, opening and fitting is an editable named SceneAct asset.

from sceneact import *

import math
from mathutils import Vector

FRONT_Y, BACK_Y = -8.0, 9.0
ROOM_H = 4.35

OLD_TARGET = (0.0, 4.2, 0.40)

yellow = (.98, .72, .025)

room = Asset('Architecture')
room.include('floor', box((ROOM_W, 17, .12), center=(0, .5, -.06), color=floor_col))
room.include('ceiling', box((ROOM_W, 17, .12), center=(0, .5, ROOM_H+.06),
                            color=(.88, .89, .84)))
for s in (-1, 1):
    x = s * ROOM_W / 2
    room.include('upper_wall_%s' % s,
        box((.12, 17, ROOM_H-1.05), center=(x, .5, 2.70), color=cream))
    room.include('yellow_lower_wall_%s' % s,
        box((.13, 17, 1.05), center=(x-s*.008, .5, .525), color=yellow))
room.include('rear_wall', box((ROOM_W, .15, ROOM_H),
                              center=(0, 9, ROOM_H/2), color=cream))
scene.include('architecture', room)

tiles = Asset('Floor tile joints')
for i in range(-7, 8):
    tiles.include('long_%d' % i,
        box((.010, 17, .004), center=(i*.65, .5, .004), color=(.62,.54,.43)))
for i in range(27):
    tiles.include('cross_%d' % i,
        box((ROOM_W, .010, .004), center=(0, -8+i*.65, .005), color=(.62,.54,.43)))
scene.include('floor_joints', tiles)

openings = Asset('Side windows and doors')
for s in (-1, 1):
    inner = s * (ROOM_W/2-.075)
    for j, y in enumerate((-6.2, -2.3, 1.5, 5.0)):
        w = Asset('Window %s %s' % (s, j))
        w.include('dark_reveal', box((.028, 1.25, 2.54),
                  center=(inner-s*.015, y, 2.04), color=(.27,.23,.16)))
        w.include('bright_pane', box((.03, 1.05, 2.30),
                  center=(inner-s*.035, y, 2.06), color=(1,1,.92)))
        for dy in (-.60, .60):
            w.include('jamb_%s' % dy, box((.075,.075,2.55),
                      center=(inner-s*.06,y+dy,2.04), color=brown))
        for z in (.78, 2.94, 3.29):
            w.include('crossbar_%s' % z, box((.08,1.25,.065),
                      center=(inner-s*.065,y,z), color=brown))
        openings.include('window_%s_%s' % (s,j), w)
    for j,y in enumerate((-4.25, 2.95)):
        d = Asset('Door %s %s' % (s,j))
        d.include('leaf', box((.055,.82,2.45),

def student_station(name, x, y, width=1.42, depth=.62):
    a = Asset(name)
    a.include('top', box((width,depth,.09), center=(x,y,.79), color=wood_top))
    a.include('apron', box((width-.08,.055,.15),
                           center=(x,y-depth/2+.045,.67), color=wood))
    for sx in (-1,1):
        for sy in (-1,1):
            a.include('leg_%s_%s' % (sx,sy), box((.058,.058,.73),
                      center=(x+sx*(width/2-.075),y+sy*(depth/2-.075),.37),
                      color=wood))
    a.include('bench_seat', box((width*.83,.27,.06),
                                 center=(x,y-.47,.43), color=(.18,.14,.10)))
    for sx in (-1,1):
        a.include('bench_leg_%s' % sx, box((.055,.055,.39),
                  center=(x+sx*width*.34,y-.47,.21), color=wood))

    a = Asset(name)
    body = ball(.5, center=(x,y,.28*scale), color=color)
    body.resize((.72*scale,.43*scale,1.08*scale))
    a.include('rounded_body', body)
    a.include('front_pocket', box((.27*scale,.035*scale,.22*scale),
              center=(x,y-.12*scale,.17*scale),
              color=tuple(v*.72 for v in color)))
    a.include('handle', rod(.017*scale, start=(x-.1*scale,y,.55*scale),
                            end=(x+.1*scale,y,.55*scale), color=dark))
    a.include('strap', rod(.018*scale, start=(x+.16*scale,y,.40*scale),
                           end=(x+.27*scale,y-.07*scale,.03), color=dark))
    return a

    ('foreground_blue',1.65,-5.55,(.01,.22,.50),1.05),
    ('central_black',.20,-3.65,(.025,.04,.04),.8),

    ('middle_blue',1.9,1.3,(.01,.26,.43),.55)]:

    f = Asset(name)
    f.include('downrod', rod(.035, start=(x,y,4.35), end=(x,y,3.92),
                             color=(.19,.18,.16)))
    f.include('hub', ball(.13, center=(x,y,3.90), color=(.19,.18,.16)))
    for k in range(3):
        ang = 2*math.pi*k/3+.2
        blade = box((1.25,.15,.035),
                    center=(x+.64*math.cos(ang),y+.64*math.sin(ang),3.89),
                    color=(.20,.19,.17))
        blade.turn('+z', math.degrees(ang))
        f.include('blade_%d' % k, blade)
    return f

def projection_table(label):
    bpy.context.view_layer.update()
    cam = sc.camera
    dg = bpy.context.evaluated_depsgraph_get()
    proj = cam.calc_matrix_camera(dg, x=512, y=340,
        scale_x=sc.render.pixel_aspect_x, scale_y=sc.render.pixel_aspect_y)
    print(label)
    for name,p,ref in landmarks:
        clip = proj @ cam.matrix_world.inverted() @ Vector((*p,1.0))
        uv = None if clip.w <= 1e-8 else (
            .5*(clip.x/clip.w+1), .5*(1-clip.y/clip.w))
        print('%-22s reference=%s projected=%s' %
              (name,ref,None if uv is None else tuple(round(v,3) for v in uv)))

SceneAct API (all coordinates in a world frame with Z up; angles in degrees):
from sceneact import *
Scene(name='Scene'), Asset(name='Asset'), Part(name, *nodes)
parent.include(name, node) attaches an asset/part while preserving its world position.
parent.members[name] retrieves a child; parent.remove(name) detaches it.
node.clone() returns an independent subtree. scene.replicate(name, new_name) duplicates an asset.
box(size=(x,y,z), center=(x,y,z), color=(r,g,b), opacity=1)
ball(radius, center=(0,0,0), color=(1,1,1), opacity=1)
rod(radius, start=(x,y,z), end=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
rod(radius, length=h, center=(0,0,0), axis='+z', color=(1,1,1))
fillet_box(size=(x,y,z), radius=r, center=(x,y,z), color=(1,1,1))
sweep_tube(points=[(x,y,z), ...], radius=.03, color=(1,1,1))
assemble(nodes, name='Assembly') groups shapes without merging their meshes.
fuse(*nodes), subtract(base,*cutters), overlap(*nodes), exclusive(left,right) construct solids.
node.move(offset), node.turn(axis, degrees, pivot=None), node.resize(factors, pivot=None)
modify a node and its descendants. node.turn(euler=(rx,ry,rz)) applies X, then Y, then Z.
Default rotation/scale pivot is the geometry's world-space bounding-box center.
shifted(node, offset), turned(node, axis, degrees, pivot=None, euler=None),
resized(node, factors, pivot=None) perform the same operations on independent copies.
node.paint(color, opacity=1) applies color to the subtree; node.rgba reads its finish.
node.centroid, node.dimensions, node.limits give AABB center, size, (minimum,maximum).
node.landmark('top'), node.landmark('front_left_bottom') return bounding-box anchors.
node.extreme(direction) returns a support point; projected_span(node,direction) returns bounds
along a unit direction; projected_width(node,direction) returns their difference.
snap(node, target, source_anchor='bottom', target_anchor='top', offset=(0,0,0)) returns a copy.
A target can also be a world point; then omit target_anchor.
abut(node, target, axis='+z', gap=0) places a copy after a target boundary.
center_on(node, target, axes=('x','y','z')) aligns selected center coordinates.
offset_at(node, reference, offsets) positions selected coordinates; None preserves a coordinate.
repeat_line(nodes, axis='+x', spacing=1) uses equal center spacing, keeping the first fixed.
pile(nodes, axis='+z', gap=0) spaces bounding surfaces, keeping the first fixed.
lattice(nodes, rows=None, columns=None, spacing=(1,1), plane='xy', center=(0,0,0), order='row-major')
orbit(nodes, radius, axis='+z', center=(0,0,0), start=0, sweep=360, orient=False, rotation_offset=0)
Layout functions return assemblies of independent copies.
scene.bind(source,target,source_anchor='bottom',target_anchor='top',offset=(0,0,0))
registers a persistent relation between scene members; scene.settle() updates dependencies.
realize(scene) settles constraints and creates Blender geometry, clearing Blender first.
set_view(position,target,lens=35,sensor=36,shift=(0,0)) creates the active camera.
area_emitter(position,power=500,size=5,target=(0,0,0),color=(1,1,1)) creates an area light.
Call realize before setting the camera and lighting. Estimate the input viewpoint yourself.
